recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Handle future resource-specific element-order complaints through their own issues because FHIR-5680 established and was applied as the general W5 ordering policy.
issue_request: FHIR-5680 asked for common resource element ordering to be made consistent; its Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution required W5 mappings, W5-order alignment with W5-mapped elements first while allowing related elements to be intermixed, application to FMM 3 resources, and consistency with conformance resources.
initial_application: Historical commits 102c1eb84e and a60d10808 explicitly mention #5680 and reordered ValueSet and Observation/resource/example source; a60d10808 also added the source/w5.ini comment that the order is the correct resource design/XML instance order. Commit 7524d34ddd later overhauled W5 categorization and added conformance/workflow categories.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini lists fivews as an active logical pattern, source/w5.html and source/qa.html retain W5/QA render hooks, publish.ini publishes w5.html, and current source/w5.ini maps ordered W5 keys to the FiveWs pattern. Later source refactors and the 2025 W5 cleanup preserved this machinery. Jira search found later resource-specific order issues but they are separate same-policy audits, not necessary to decide FHIR-5680.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current specification already has the authoritative W5/FiveWs ordering configuration in build scope; adding prose or reordering arbitrary current resources would be speculative and outside the bounded seed decision.
